shortcut_name: direct reduction to bipartite graph coloring
evidence: "color = [-1] * n # -1 uncolored, 0 -> value 1, 1 -> value 2"; "bipartite colour"; "Check the constraint: |a³ - b³| = 7 where a,b ∈ {1,2}"
affordance_in_statement: Every satellite ... must be assigned a tuning parameter, which is an integer chosen from {1, 2}. Whenever two satellites are involved in a proximity hazard, the absolute difference between the cubes of their tuning parameters must be exactly 7
removal_suggestion: This cannot be removed without changing the immutable domain or required difference: for values 1 and 2, the condition is exactly |1³ − 2³| = 7, so every hazard forces opposite assignments. Only the presentation can be obscured, for example by describing the two tuning modes and their compatibility rule indirectly rather than displaying the arithmetic equation.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treat the two allowed parameter values as the two colors of a graph and check bipartiteness.
Use BFS two-coloring, with the graph condition interpreted as a bipartite-color constraint.
Recognize that the cubic condition over the two-value domain forces endpoints to receive different colors.
Solve the hazards as a standard graph bipartiteness problem using two colors.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: "color = [0] ..." together with the two-color BFS/DFS structure

common_affordance: Because the only allowed values are 1 and 2 and |1³ − 2³| = 7, every hazard requires unequal endpoint values, making the task exactly bipartite graph recognition and coloring.
recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat this common shortcut: it is the intrinsic structure of the stated constraint.
